ai.literal: What is called truthfulness, if you ask, is the speaking of words free from even the slightest harm to anyone.
ai.translation: If one asks what truthfulness is, it is the speaking of words that are free from even the slightest harm to any living being.
ai.modern: வாய்மை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எது என்றால், அது எவ்விதத்திலும் யாருக்கும் தீமை இல்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசுவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the nature of truthfulness is defined not by literal accuracy, but by its impact. The author explains that true speech is that which is completely free from causing harm to any being. The phrase 'yātoṉṟum tīmai ilāta' emphasizes that even the smallest amount of harm must be absent. Therefore, the moral value of speech is determined by its benevolence and its capacity to prevent harm.

ai.literal: Even falsehood is of the status of truth, if it yields fault-free goodness.
ai.translation: Even falsehood has the nature of truth, if it produces pure, faultless good.
ai.modern: குற்றம் இல்லாத நன்மையை விளைவிக்கும் என்றால், பொய் சொல்லுவதும் வாய்மையின் தன்மையைப் பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet presents a profound ethical perspective on truth. It states that even an untruth (பொய்மையும்) can be elevated to the status of truth (வாய்மை இடத்த) under one condition: if it results in completely faultless good (புரைதீர்ந்த நன்மை பயக்கும் எனின்). The key words 'புரைதீர்ந்த நன்மை' emphasize that the outcome must be entirely free from harm or bad intentions. Thus, the moral value of speech is judged not just by literal accuracy, but by the benevolent impact it has on others.

ai.literal: Do not lie about that which one's own mind knows; after lying, one's own mind itself will burn oneself.
ai.translation: Do not tell a lie about what your own mind knows to be true; if you do lie, your own conscience will burn you.
ai.modern: தன் மனதுக்குத் தெரிந்த உண்மையை மறைத்துப் பொய் சொல்லக் கூடாது; அப்படிப் பொய் சொன்னால், தன் மனமே தன்னை வருத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of conscience in upholding truthfulness. It advises that one must never speak a lie against what their own heart or mind knows to be true. If a person goes against their inner knowledge and lies, their own conscience will continuously torment and burn them with guilt. The word 'neñcu' (heart or mind) here represents the internal witness of truth, and 'cuṭum' (will burn) vividly describes the painful heat of self-reproach.

ai.literal: By the mind without lying if one conducts oneself, of the world's people in the minds of all, he will exist.
ai.translation: If one conducts oneself without deceit in one's own heart, one will dwell in the hearts of all people in the world.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தன் நெஞ்சறியப் பொய் சொல்லாமல் வாழ்ந்தால், அவர் உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லாருடைய மனங்களிலும் வாழ்வார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the profound power of inner truthfulness. If a person lives their life without harboring falsehood in their own mind, they earn a permanent place in the hearts of everyone in the world. True truthfulness is not merely about spoken words, but about absolute inner honesty. By being pure in thought, such a person becomes universally loved and remembered.

ai.literal: With mind truth if [one] speaks, with penance charity those who do than, superior.
ai.translation: If one speaks the truth with all one's heart, they are superior to those who perform both penance and charity.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தன் மனப்பூர்வமாக உண்மையைச் சொன்னால், அவர் தவமும் தானமும் செய்பவர்களை விடச் சிறந்தவர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the virtue of speaking the truth with the traditional religious practices of penance and charity. The phrase 'மனத்தொடு வாய்மை மொழியின்' highlights that truthfulness must come from a sincere and pure mind, not just as a superficial utterance. The poet declares that a person who practices such heartfelt truthfulness is superior ('தலை') to those who perform rigorous austerities ('தவத்தொடு') and give away wealth ('தானம்'). Thus, inner truthfulness is elevated above even the most celebrated external spiritual and moral acts.

ai.literal: Not-lying like fame there-is-not; effortlessly all virtue it-will-give.
ai.translation: There is no fame equal to that of never lying; without any effort, it will yield every other virtue.
ai.modern: பொய் சொல்லாமல் இருத்தலைப் போன்ற புகழ் வேறு இல்லை; அது ஒருவருக்கு எந்தவிதமான சோர்வும் முயற்சியும் இல்லாமல் எல்லா அறங்களையும் தரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet highlights the supreme value of truthfulness by stating that there is no greater glory than maintaining it. The word 'poyyāmai' refers to the practice of never uttering falsehoods. The poet asserts that this single practice is so powerful that it effortlessly ('eyyāmai', meaning without fatigue or struggle) brings about all other virtues ('ellā aṟamum') to a person. Thus, by simply adhering to truth, one naturally attains the fruits of all other righteous deeds without having to strive for them individually.

ai.literal: Non-lying, non-lying if practiced, other virtues not doing, not doing is good.
ai.translation: If one consistently practices the virtue of truthfulness without fail, then even if one does not perform any other virtues, it is still good.
ai.modern: பொய்யாமை என்னும் அறத்தை ஒருவன் தொடர்ந்து கடைப்பிடித்தால், அவன் வேறு எந்த அறங்களையும் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதுவே அவனுக்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme status of truthfulness, defined here as the avoidance of falsehood. By repeating the words 'பொய்யாமை' (non-lying) and 'செய்யாமை' (not doing), the poet uses emphasis to show that truthfulness alone is sufficient for a virtuous life. If a person can strictly adhere to speaking the truth under all circumstances, they do not need to perform other moral or ritualistic deeds. The simple act of avoiding falsehood is so powerful that it encompasses and surpasses all other virtues.

ai.literal: Exterior purity by water is established; interior purity by truthfulness is seen.
ai.translation: Outward purity is achieved by water, while inward purity is manifested by truthfulness.
ai.modern: உடலின் புறத்தூய்மை நீரினால் உண்டாகும்; உள்ளத்தின் அகத்தூய்மை வாய்மையால் (உண்மையால்) வெளிப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a clear contrast between physical cleanliness and moral purity. The author explains that while water is sufficient to cleanse the external body (puram), it cannot wash the inner self or mind (akam). Inner purity can only be achieved and made visible to others through truthfulness (vaymai) in thought, speech, and action. Thus, truthfulness is presented as the ultimate purifying agent for the human soul, just as water is for the physical body.

ai.literal: All lamps are not lamps; to the noble, the unlying lamp indeed is the lamp.
ai.translation: All external lamps that shed light are not true lamps; to the virtuous, the lamp of truthfulness, which never lies, is the only true lamp.
ai.modern: புற இருளை நீக்கும் எல்லா விளக்குகளும் உண்மையான விளக்குகள் அல்ல; சான்றோர்களுக்குப் பொய் சொல்லாத வாய்மை என்னும் விளக்கே உண்மையான விளக்காகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical lamps with the spiritual light of truthfulness. The poet states that ordinary lamps, which merely dispel physical darkness, are not considered true lights by noble minds. For the virtuous, the only real lamp is truthfulness, referred to here as the 'unlying lamp' (poyyā viḷakku). While physical lights can be extinguished and only illuminate the outside, the light of truth shines eternally within, guiding a person's character and dispelling the darkness of ignorance and falsehood.

ai.literal: Among those things we have seen as truth, there is not any other thing of any measure that is better than truthfulness.
ai.translation: Among all the truths we have discerned in our experience, we have found nothing of any measure that is better than truthfulness.
ai.modern: நாம் உண்மையாக ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்தவற்றுள், வாய்மையை விடச் சிறந்ததாக வேறு எந்த ஒரு நற்பண்பும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The poet declares that of all the values and truths experienced and realized in life, there is nothing superior to truthfulness. The phrase 'யாம் மெய்யாக் கண்டவற்றுள்' emphasizes personal, experiential realization rather than mere theoretical knowledge. The word 'எனைத்தொன்றும்' stresses that truthfulness stands absolutely supreme, with no other virtue exceeding it even in the slightest measure. By comparing truthfulness to all other known virtues, the couplet establishes it as the ultimate and most beneficial principle of human life.
